name: Sirius Satellite Radio (Tundra) — Historical (2000-2016)
description: Historic satellite-radio constellation in the 24-hour Tundra orbit (~25,000 × 35,786 km) at the 63.4° critical inclination. The three original Sirius FM satellites (FM-1, FM-2, FM-3) each dwelt over CONUS for roughly two-thirds of every orbit, giving urban-canyon receivers elevation angles a geostationary signal couldn't match. Sirius FM-1 launched from Baikonur in 2000 on a Proton-K; FM-2 and FM-3 followed. The company merged with XM Radio in 2008 to form Sirius XM. The Tundra-orbit constellation was decommissioned in 2016, and Sirius XM now operates a fleet of ~7 geostationary satellites.
